title: Sweden vs Poland: The Clash That Decides the Nations League Path
seoTitle: Sweden vs Poland: Nations League path decided
subtitle: Understand the Strawberry Arena showdown that could alter the Euro 2028 route
excerpt: The Sweden vs Poland match on September 28 carries real weight in Nations League B, with promotion, relegation, and Euro 2028 access at stake.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Monday, September 28, Sweden hosts Poland at 3:45 PM (Brasília time) at the Strawberry Arena in Solna, for the second round of Nations League B. The encounter gains prominence because the three points could define the fight for promotion to League A and pave the way for Euro 2028.

Match Significance

Six months after eliminating Poland 3-2 in the World Cup playoff semi-final, the Swedes face their old rival again in a group stage context. The clash is worth decisive points for both sides, who are still looking to consolidate their positions in League B.

Team Form

Sweden entered the Nations League with a 2-1 triumph over Romania in the first round, boosted by the morale of their playoff victory. Coach Graham Potter adopted a 4-4-2 formation that favors the Alexander Isak-Viktor Gyokeres partnership. Poland, led by Jan Urban, started with a 0-0 draw against Bosnia and has accumulated few goals, reflecting doubts about the physical condition of key players.

Probable Lineups

For Sweden, the probable formation (4-4-2) includes Johansson; Holm, Starfelt, Lindelöf, and Stroud; Bernhardsson, Bergvall, Ayari, and Nanasi; Gyokeres and Isak, under Potter's command. On the Polish side, the 4-4-1-1 could feature Bułka; Cash, Bednarek, Potulski, and Frankowski; Skóraś, Nowak, Zieliński, and Zalewski; Szymański; and Lewandowski, managed by Urban.

Critical Factors of the Clash

The head-to-head history shows an average of four goals per match, indicating an open game. The home advantage, combined with Sweden's offensive volume, could pressure the Polish defense, which has shown fragility on aerial balls. On the other hand, Zieliński's creativity and Lewandowski's presence, even if limited, could be decisive for Poland.

Odds and Betting Expectations

Bookmakers place a Swedish victory at 1.91, a draw at 3.60, and a Polish victory at 3.70. The goals market offers options like “over 2.5” at 1.65 and “both teams to score” at 1.65, reflecting the tendency for high-scoring games between the two teams.

What's at Stake

A Swedish victory would open a five-point lead in Group B4, placing them in a comfortable position to seek promotion to League A. For Poland, the match is an opportunity to recover points and keep alive the hope of advancing towards Euro 2028, despite an inconsistent run of results.
